newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end bourse trade sharply lower. [CORRECTED 14:35 GMT]
newsitem.headline: German shares end bourse trade sharply lower. [CORRECTED 14:35 GMT]

text.p: German shares generally declined in floor trading on Monday as the DAX index fell 2.69 percent on interest rate concerns and pessimism left over from late electronic trading on Friday.
The DAX index of 30 German blue-chip stocks ended floor trade down 111.85 points (corrects from 118 points) at 4,296.94, its first close below the 4,300 level since July 22.
"Everyone is unsettled, worried about interest rates," one trader said.
German blue-chips were down across the board.
Volumes were heaviest in banks stocks, as Deutsche Bank AG slipped 4.85 marks to 117.30, Commerzbank AG fell 1.30 to 61.35, and Dresdner Bank AG fell 3.70 to 80.20.
Bayerische Hypo-Bank, soon to merge with fellow Bavarian bank Vereinsbank was among the chief losers in floor trade, down 3.75 marks at 72.20 marks.
Chemical giant BASF AG closed down 45 pfennigs at 70.20 marks and Bayer AG was down 1.05 at 75.45 marks, while pharmaceutical group Schering AG was down 3.70 marks at 199 marks.
Airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG was down 1.50 at 34.80 marks.
The market was weak from its opening, with little new economic data arriving to boost trading in the wake of a one percent drop in the IBIS DAX in late computer dealings on Friday.
Some support for the market came from the dollar's strength at 1.87 marks, which has been behind much of the market's rise in recent months as it boosts German exports.
